title: Attribute token consumption for speculative KV warmups and background prefetches
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
We currently perform speculative KV warmups (background prefetches of model KV cache and prefix-level warming) to reduce tail latency for incoming requests. Those warmups generate GPU token work and sometimes form coalesced microbatches. Billing and quota accounting for these warmups is inconsistent: sometimes warmup tokens are attributed to the triggering request, sometimes to an internal warmup pool, and sometimes are effectively unaccounted for. This ticket defines a reproducible attribution policy and implements changes to ensure warmup-generated token usage is visible, billable, and correctly affects rate limits/quotas.
problem_statement:
Problem details:
- Speculative warmups are run by multiple components (router prefetch, workload-driven prefetcher, on-deck warmers). Warmups may execute as separate RPCs, piggyback onto other microbatches, or be collapsed into internal coalesced batches.
- Current metering pipeline lacks stable provenance metadata for warmup work. Without provenance we can neither reliably charge customers nor reason about quota throttles.
- Edge cases: (1) warmup happens long before a real request (no clear owner); (2) warmup is triggered by a request but executed asynchronously later (owner unclear); (3) multi-tenant KV warmups that touch shared model cache on dedicated nodes.
- Rate limiter only tracks request tokens; warmup tokens sometimes bypass quota buckets which can cause silent capacity drift and surprise chargebacks.
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance criteria:
1) Every warmup-generated token meter event must include a provenance tag: warmup_origin (router|prefetcher|scheduler), initiating_request_id (if available), and warmup_timestamp.
2) If a warmup can be correlated to a real request that arrives within the configured correlation_window (default 3s), token usage is attributed to that request's customer/route for billing and quota.
3) If no correlated request exists, warmup tokens are attributed to a configurable warmup budget owned by the customer (if feature enabled) or to a separate internal warmup charge account depending on tenant settings.
4) Rate limiter treats warmup_budget tokens against a distinct warmup allowance first, then falls back to customer quota when warmup_budget is exhausted.
5) Console adds warmup token line-items in per-route/monthly billing and exposes warmup metrics (tokens, warmup_hits, warmup_misses, attribution_ratio).
6) Backfill tests that simulate coalesced microbatches with mixed provenance must show deterministic attribution.
proposed_solution:
Implementation plan:
- Metadata & Telemetry:
  * Add provenance fields to internal request envelope: provenance.type (warmup|request), provenance.subsystem (router|prefetcher|scheduler), provenance.initiating_request_id (nullable), provenance.correlation_window_ms (int).
  * Metering pipeline to emit warmup_flag and provenance.* fields as part of token events.
- Attribution rules (server-side):
  * If initiating_request_id present and a live request with same id arrives within correlation_window -> attribute to that request owner and route.
  * Else, consult tenant setting: if tenant has warmup_pool_enabled -> bill to tenant warmup budget (separate meter bucket).
  * Else bill to internal platform warmup account and surface in invoice as "Platform-warmup" with attribution metadata for debugging.
  * For shared nodes (Dedicated): when warmup touches cross-tenant cache keys, attribute proportional token share to active tenants based on recent request token weights over last T minutes (configurable, default 10).
- Rate limiting integration:
  * Introduce warmup allowance per-tenant (configurable monthly allotment). Warmup requests consume warmup allowance before customer quota.
  * When warmup allowance exhausted, warmup requests should either be rate-limited (if tenant preference=throttle) or charged to main quota.
- Metering/Coalescing changes:
  * When microbatches are coalesced, preserve provenance vector: a list of provenance entries and associated token counts. Metering pipeline must accept and record multi-provenance events and apply attribution rules atomically.
  * For billing, collapse multi-provenance microbatch events into per-provenance token counts before invoice generation.
technical_notes:
Engineering details and trade-offs:
- Correlation_window: 3s default minimizes false-positive owner attribution but may miss legitimate near-future requests. We will make this tenant-configurable.
- Cost of storing provenance vectors: might increase metering event payloads. We will compress provenance vectors and only keep aggregated per-batch counts downstream.
- Proportional attribution on shared cache: this heuristic prevents free-riding but is approximate; add hooks for manual dispute resolution in billing console.
- Backwards compatibility: legacy meter consumers that can't handle provenance should receive a fallback aggregated token event with attribute=unknown. New consumers can use detailed provenance.
- Security: provenance fields do not contain sensitive content (no prompt text). Ensure we never leak initiating request prompts in meter events.
- Perf: enriching every warmup with provenance may add ~0.2ms to routing path; measurement will be done in a canary cluster.
- Edge-case: speculative warmups triggered by autoscaling or offline schedulers will have subsystem=scheduler and initiating_request_id=null.
rollout_plan:
Rollout steps:
1) Telemetry + metering pipeline change in a feature-flagged branch: emit provenance fields and warmup_flag. (Canary group only)
2) Implement attribution logic in billing/charge-generator as feature-flagged.
3) Wire warmup allowance config into tenant settings and default policy.
4) Run a 2-week canary on non-production fleet and collect metrics: attribution_ratio, warmup_token_pct, quota_impact.
5) Enable for 10% of production traffic; verify no billing regressions and validate console reports.
6) Full rollout after 7 days of stable metrics and finance sign-off.
7) Post-rollout: run retrospective and open follow-up tickets for disputes and UX improvements.
test_plan:
Tests to run:
- Unit tests for provenance propagation and correlation logic.
- Integration tests that simulate: (a) warmup immediately preceding a request, (b) warmup long before request, (c) coalesced microbatch with mixed provenance.
- Load test to measure overhead and ensure metering throughput.
- Billing e2e test: generate invoice preview showing warmup line items and check math for proportional attribution.
- Rate limiter tests for warmup allowance depletion and fallback behaviors.
- Chaos test: simulate warmup RPC failures and ensure no silent token loss.
outstanding_questions:
Open decisions:
- Default policy for tenants without a warmup pool: bill to customer main quota or to platform account? (Finance leaning: bill customer by default unless tenant opts into warmup pool).
- Correlation window tuning: start 3s, but we need perf experiments to find sweet spot per-region.
- Shared node attribution window length for proportional sharing (default 10 minutes).
- UX: how much detail to show in invoices—line items per-warmup can be noisy. Propose aggregated monthly warmup line-item per-route.
